signals.source_text: Traditional aerial firefighting is broken. Here is how I propose to fix it. Dropping water from ultra-low altitudes endangers flight crews and frequently loses efficiency due to fluid evaporation before reaching the fire perimeter. I have developed a method for high-altitude structured water release from 150 meters, integrated with automatic navigation systems. Key Technical Advantages: 📍 High Precision: Phased, targeted agent distribution along active fire edges — even at night and under light smoke conditions. 🛡 Crew Safety: Flight operations occur at a safe altitude, well above extreme thermal updrafts and hazardous terrain. 🌲 Maximum Efficiency: Optimized drop physics maximize fluid volume reaching the ground. Physics works the same everywhere, making this technology universally applicable. Given the urgency of the global fire crisis, I am currently preparing this solution for deployment in North America (Canada & US) with a vision for global implementation. I'm looking for strategic R&D partners, grant co-applicants, and venture investors to help scale development. I also have a portfolio of over ten engineering solutions focused on enhancing fire suppression in wildland and complex urban environments. 📄 Full technical layout and details are in the attached document below. How is your region adapting aerial tactics for this year’s fire season? Let's discuss in the comments. #WildfireSuppression #AerialFirefighting #CanadaWildfires #USFirefighting #AviationSafety
